name: immovability

attributes.attribute: a folkloric motif where moved sacred stones return by their own power
an early British historian who recorded the belief

sources: Grinsell, Leslie V. Folklore of Prehistoric Sites in Britain. London: David & Charles, 1976.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Immovability is a folkloric motif. It is also called automatic return. The great stone monuments of the pre-Celtic people impressed the new settlers. Many superstitions grew around these sites. The beliefs preserved the monuments for millennia. One belief was recorded by the early British historian Nennius. If a stone was moved from its sacred place, it returned the next day by its own power. Some stones would hurt or kill the thief as they returned.
objective: Document the folkloric motif of immovability, or automatic return.
key_results: Record the superstitions around pre-Celtic stone monuments.
Record the belief that moved stones return by their own power.
Note the record of this by the historian Nennius.
evidence: Monaghan, P. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore (2008): immovability entry.
